channel.title: Diffbrief · Architecture
channel.description: Daily architecture stories worth an engineer's time.

item.title: Replit migrates hundreds of millions of projects to a microVM sandbox engine
item.description: Replit rewrote its sandbox engine around microVMs, changing the isolation boundary while migrating hundreds of millions of projects without data loss. The account covers the trade-offs involved in securing and scaling sandboxes for coding agents.

item.title: Halley adds predictive control across optical AI data-center networks
item.description: Halley combines controllers for laser reserves, switch scheduling, thermal control and risk-based triage, reporting effective goodput rising from 65.2% to 76.5% in simulations. The work connects failure prediction and resource control to accelerator-cluster network throughput.

item.title: Greenlight’s 30-plus agents resolve over 90% of security cases autonomously
item.description: Greenlight says its Luna system resolves over 90% of up to 4,000 monthly security and risk cases, using more than 30 specialized agents and episodic memory. The production architecture and metrics offer concrete lessons for autonomous workflows in regulated settings.

item.title: Firecracker guest takes over a live vCPU thread to reach host root
item.description: The exploit uses host-memory access to locate Firecracker, alter a vCPU thread's saved state, and execute a chosen call on the host. It demonstrates a serious microVM isolation failure relevant to anyone running untrusted workloads.

item.title: Waymark compiles durable workflows into stackless VM bytecode
item.description: Waymark walks workflow code's AST and compiles control flow to stackless VM bytecode rather than replaying past state; it currently supports Python. That design is worth comparing with durable-execution systems such as Temporal and DBOS.

item.title: An ECS Fargate MCP server centralizes agent access to a data lake
item.description: The NASC team built a serverless MCP gateway to connect agents to enterprise data without duplicating integrations and access-control logic. Centralizing that boundary can simplify onboarding as agents and data sources multiply.

item.title: Discord is moving its desktop client from Electron to Rust
item.description: Discord says the move removes Electron and React Native from its client, with desktop and mobile sharing Rust code while mobile retains native UI. The migration is a useful architecture example for teams balancing resource use with cross-platform code sharing.

item.title: A blog replaces Route 53 GeoDNS with Bunny's scriptable DNS
item.description: The author moves a blog's geo-aware DNS from Route 53 to Bunny, citing per-zone, query, health-check and DNSSEC key costs, and describes CDN and DNS configuration choices. The migration offers practical trade-offs for engineers managing global delivery and cloud costs.

item.title: Shopify Reflex lets agents test native mobile apps without emulators
item.description: Reflex runs app logic headlessly and exposes each screen's state and actions, letting agents test behavior without a simulator and share a test suite across iOS and Android. Its architecture tackles feedback-loop speed and cross-platform consistency in agent-written apps.

item.title: Rivet runs agent workloads as lightweight, S3-backed actors
item.description: Rivet gives each agent a long-lived actor with in-memory state, WebSockets, durable SQLite backed by S3, and hibernation when idle. Its actor-based alternative to a heavyweight sandbox is a useful architecture to examine for scalable agent workloads.

item.title: Dropbox agents use controlled workspaces and reversible file changes
item.description: Dropbox’s agent can organize folders, rename files and prepare materials, while permissions, recorded changes, review and undo constrain its actions. The architecture offers practical lessons for safely giving agents access to users’ files.

item.title: NVIDIA's factory blueprint coordinates specialist agents with operator review
item.description: The reference architecture combines a manager agent, persistent memory, access policies, and specialist agents for inspection, fleet management, and root-cause analysis. Its production-line example shows how agent actions can be coordinated while reserving decisions for operator review.

item.title: Indegene builds a governed agent for enterprise data-quality rules
item.description: Indegene’s Data Quality Agent generates context-aware rules, validates them, and produces ready-to-run SQL and Python under centralized human governance. The pattern shows how an agent can help scale data-quality work while keeping review in the workflow.

item.title: Multi-agent systems add coordination failures beyond single-agent reasoning
item.description: The piece frames coordination as the main engineering burden when splitting work across agents and focuses on failures in unattended production use. That distinction matters when deciding whether a multi-agent architecture is worth operating.

item.title: DataGrip embeds DuckDB to query across database connections
item.description: JetBrains embedded DuckDB and used custom table functions to connect cross-database queries to DataGrip’s existing query execution, rather than building a new engine. It’s a practical example of extending an established product by embedding a specialized engine.

item.title: GitHub redesigns Git storage for thousands of agents pushing to one repository
item.description: GitHub says its new Git storage architecture supports thousands of agents pushing to a single repository, but the excerpt gives no implementation details. The scale target makes the design relevant to teams supporting highly concurrent automation.

item.title: Unplanned Postgres failover must detect outages and choose a safe replica
item.description: Neki’s failover process must determine whether a primary is dead or merely unreachable, then select a replica without a final WAL position from the primary. Those uncertainties shape safe failover design in distributed databases.

item.title: TUI uses Bedrock to scale threat modeling across more than 100 teams
item.description: TUI built an AI-powered threat-modeling system after manual reviews took 4–6 hours and the team could complete only 3–4 sessions monthly. The case is relevant to engineers automating security review across many product teams.

item.title: ByteDance USDB reuses storage maintenance across recommendation workloads
item.description: USDB combines time-based CascadeLSM compaction, shared persistent files, partial dumps and a hybrid columnar format for streaming, batch, training and inference workloads. Production migrations report an 85.8% reduction, though the excerpt cuts off before naming the metric; the design offers concrete storage patterns for recommendation systems.

item.title: NVIDIA's operations agent correlates failures across SuperPOD layers
item.description: Specialist agents investigate compute, network, hardware and scheduling failures, with read-only recommendations surfaced for SRE review. The design offers practical lessons in agent boundaries, cross-layer diagnosis and trust for production operations.

item.title: Figma built Nimbus to manage tens of thousands of sandboxes for untrusted code
item.description: Figma says its AI products need tens of thousands of sandboxes and that Nimbus makes them fast, reliable, and manageable for product teams and operators. The case is directly relevant to designing isolation infrastructure for systems that execute untrusted code.

item.title: U Mobile applies agents to multi-system telecom operations
item.description: Resolving a subscriber’s failed data add-on purchase can require coordinating interface logs, business-support APIs, and policy knowledge bases before a response is drafted. The case highlights the integration challenge behind automating operational support across systems.

item.title: Mercari projects 50%+ cost savings by replacing legacy VDI for customer service
item.description: Mercari chose Chrome Enterprise Premium and Chromebooks for a customer-service environment handling sensitive data, aiming to reduce VDI costs and overlapping data-loss controls. The migration offers a concrete security and operations trade-off for teams designing managed work environments.

item.title: Anthropic's source-control bottleneck is repository setup and change recording
item.description: As coding agents generate more code, repository downloads, workspace preparation and recording changes have become bottlenecks at Anthropic. The shift highlights how agent throughput can move constraints from coding into developer infrastructure.

item.title: RoboColosseum evaluates robot policies across 124 real-world sites
item.description: The distributed framework runs matched policy evaluations across locally operated robots; 5,699 pairwise comparisons found frontier agents rival specialized policies, with rankings varying sharply by embodiment. It shows how to structure reproducible, large-scale evaluation across heterogeneous deployments.

item.title: Revolut moves 2,000 engineers to self-hosted GLM for coding
item.description: A post says Revolut moved about 2,000 engineers to self-hosted GLM on 56 Nvidia B200s, at a blended $0.30 per million tokens, and reports 70% better engineering lead time. The migration offers a concrete look at how lower model costs can change usage across an engineering team.

item.title: Meta F3 merges ads features into one graph for requests needing 20,000-plus features
item.description: Meta’s feature framework compiles ads features into one merged graph, reducing execution compute for requests that can require more than 20,000 features. The design offers lessons for serving high-volume ML features efficiently.

item.title: Progressive disaster-recovery tests expose gaps that scheduled failovers miss
item.description: Scheduled exercises can verify traffic shifts and data consistency but may not test team coordination or who declares a failover; the article lays out progressive validation. This is useful for designing recovery commitments that hold up beyond rehearsed conditions.

item.title: Three recovery decisions shape disaster-recovery targets before architecture
item.description: The guide focuses on what to recover, what recovery the business needs, and what dependencies make a commitment feasible; revisiting these decisions helped turn a missed target into a successful test. Teams can use the framework before selecting a DR architecture.

item.title: Namespace builds Mac racks to launch macOS instances in seconds
item.description: Namespace describes custom Mac racks for starting macOS instances from scratch in seconds and delivering new Xcode versions within hours of release. It is a practical infrastructure case study for teams that need Macs to build and test iOS apps, including coding-agent workflows.

item.title: Webhook integrations need deduplication, buffering and reconciliation
item.description: The author traces webhook integrations from signature checks and duplicate-delivery handling to out-of-order events, bootstrap races and reconciliation. These recurring design problems matter whenever local systems mirror customer data held by third parties.

item.title: PostHog replaces DuckDB with Trino for its customer data warehouse
item.description: PostHog moved away from per-customer DuckDB instances after finding that customer workloads were larger and more complex than expected, and is rebuilding on Trino with HogLake. The account offers concrete trade-offs from redesigning a managed warehouse for scale and cost.

item.title: Cloudflare halves DNS build delay and cuts memory use by 85%
item.description: Cloudflare’s DNS Zone Builder now handles nearly three times the record-change rate described in its 2022 account, while cutting build delay in half and memory use by 85%. Its approach to incremental builds for large zones offers practical lessons for systems that turn changing data into edge-ready state.

item.title: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend for Codex-scale development
item.description: OpenAI built Pando as a Git-compatible backend for the development scale enabled by Codex. Its architecture may offer useful lessons for teams handling unusually large development workloads, though the excerpt gives no further implementation details.

item.title: NVIDIA Recovery automates distributed-training failure detection and restart
item.description: The recovery loop detects anomalies, attributes failures, isolates implicated nodes, and restarts or stops jobs under policy; monitor mode and an audit trail let operators validate behavior before enabling actions. The design shows how to introduce autonomous recovery without skipping oversight.

item.title: Circle K uses Bedrock to cut DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes
item.description: Circle K built an automated Bedrock triage system to investigate alerts across its cloud infrastructure; the headline reports triage under 15 minutes, against a prior 45–60 minutes of investigation. The case offers a concrete reference for applying AI to operational workflows at scale.

item.title: AWS outlines a disaster recovery engagement that validates recovery commitments
item.description: The guide gives steps for moving from undefined disaster-recovery targets to a validated commitment, starting with application, business and platform owners mapping the recovery boundary. Its concrete process helps teams expose missing dependency ownership before committing to recovery timelines.

item.title: AWS DRS lifecycle automation addresses stalled agents and unwanted replication
item.description: An enterprise with more than 300 Linux and Windows instances automated AWS Replication Agent installation, recovery and offboarding after network changes stalled agents and descoped servers kept replicating. The case highlights how lifecycle gaps can undermine recovery objectives and add cost.

item.title: Discord unified two video players and cut maintained code by up to 94%
item.description: Discord describes refactoring two video players into one reusable system, reducing the player code each product maintained by up to 94%. The migration offers practical lessons for simplifying shared components while making future changes safer.

item.title: Scion and Mononoke offer competing approaches to monorepo version control
item.description: A Databricks source-control engineer examines Anthropic’s Scion alongside Mononoke while their team explores options for a huge monorepo. The perspective offers useful context on version-control architecture at scale.

item.title: AlloyDB AI embedding upgrades require coordinated re-embedding and index migration
item.description: Changing embedding models requires re-embedding stored data, rebuilding indexes, and coordinating old and new models because their vector spaces are incompatible. The migration problem is central to keeping production semantic search available during model upgrades.

item.title: Uber built a gateway to connect AI agents with internal tools
item.description: The excerpt explains why general-purpose models need specialized tools to act on a company’s internal systems, and the title identifies Uber’s gateway as the solution. The architecture is relevant to teams managing many agent tools.

item.title: QA Studio adds test ownership and visibility for teams scaling agentic QA
item.description: The series moves from natural-language visual tests and CI regression suites to the organizational problem of managing tests across products and squads. Engineers building shared agent-driven QA platforms can learn which ownership and visibility problems emerge at scale.

item.title: Oracle AI Database and Google Cloud connect operational data to Gemini workflows
item.description: The expanded partnership connects Oracle operational databases with Google’s data and AI ecosystem, including BigQuery and Gemini, to give agents secure, real-time data access. The integration illustrates the data connectivity and governance layers behind enterprise agent workflows.

item.title: MoEngage connects 400 private APIs to agents through AgentCore Gateway
item.description: MoEngage needed to expose roughly 400 private APIs across seven AWS Regions without public access, model-controlled identity, or hundreds of tool definitions in agent context. The case addresses a common platform challenge: making existing services safely usable by agents at scale.

item.title: EasyProver combines recursive agents with isolated contexts and parallel search
item.description: EasyProver uses isolated agent contexts, asynchronous search, parallel tactic probing and elastic elaboration; it reports 597 of 600 NTP4VC conditions resolved and 52.7% of a harder 2,000-statement sample proved. Its architecture and evaluation offer concrete lessons for scaling verification agents.

item.title: An AgentCore platform gives teams shared identity, isolation, evaluation, and cost controls
item.description: The platform model gives workstream teams approved models and tools, short-lived identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. It offers a concrete checklist for building a governed multi-team agent platform.

item.title: Worldwide Express reports a 75% drop in freight exceptions with multi-agent automation
item.description: A Bedrock-based multi-agent system connected to the company’s transportation management system reportedly cut active exceptions by 75%, improved time-to-cash by four weeks, and saved $1 million annually. The case shows the reported operational impact of automating a high-volume business workflow.

item.title: DeltaDB versions the reasoning behind code changes made by humans and agents
item.description: DeltaDB is designed to stream code changes from people and agents while preserving the context behind them, so users can recover the reasoning and ask its author about a change. It tackles the problem of agent-generated context disappearing into harnesses, chat, or commit messages.

item.title: Azure API Connections flaws enable five full cross-tenant compromises
item.description: The flaws let attackers compromise other tenants’ API Connections and reach connected services including Key Vault and Azure SQL; the researcher says input validation is the main barrier. It is a serious cloud-isolation failure with lessons for platform architects.

item.title: Three networking bugs silenced Kubernetes APIs across GKE clusters
item.description: Three bugs across GKE, Private Service Connect, and Linux networking combined to block about 800 developers and halt clusters in europe-west; the final fix was an upstream Linux patch. The incident shows how layered failures can defeat symptom-level debugging.

item.title: NVIDIA AICR packages Dynamo inference runtimes as validated Kubernetes recipes
item.description: AICR pins GPU drivers, scheduling, health signals, and monitoring in reproducible recipes, with Dynamo routing through either its frontend or Gateway API and EPP. The runtime and deployment choices offer a concrete path to operating cache-aware inference on Kubernetes.

item.title: DoorDash cuts grocery reorder latency from 16 seconds to 2 with agents
item.description: DoorDash precomputes recurring purchase needs with batch LLM inference and deterministic validation, then uses live catalog resolution and an editable list to limit model calls. The reported latency and order-rate gains offer concrete design lessons for agentic commerce flows.

item.title: GitHub added 4 million CPU cores and 160 PB of storage to handle 7.4 billion commits
item.description: GitHub reportedly handled 7.4 billion commits in September by adding more than 4 million CPU cores and 160 PB of storage. The scale makes its capacity and storage choices relevant to engineers running large software platforms.

item.title: BMW migrated its connected-vehicle platform from x86 to Graviton
item.description: BMW's connected-vehicle platform, serving a fleet of more than 24.5 million vehicles, began moving from x86 to Arm-based compute; the team used Karpenter for flexible node provisioning. The migration patterns and tooling are relevant to large-scale platform modernization.

item.title: Stripe moved more than $1 billion in vendor payments onto Global Payouts
item.description: Stripe replaced direct bank integrations and manual bank-portal entry with a single API, using Global Payouts for more than $1 billion in payments to over 3,400 vendors. The migration offers practical lessons on consolidating market-specific payment operations as a system scales.

item.title: Kubernetes AI Conformance moves from a working group to SIG Architecture
item.description: Kubernetes AI Conformance moved from an initial Working Group into SIG Architecture as a subproject. Engineers building AI platforms on Kubernetes can track how the project is being integrated into the community's architecture work.

item.title: Sonos distributes audio over Wi-Fi to speakers with local amplifiers
item.description: The piece describes a distributed audio design that sends sound over IP to amplifiers beside each speaker, and the challenge of keeping playback synchronized over variable Wi-Fi. The reliability problem has useful parallels for systems operating over unpredictable networks.

item.title: Rack-aware scheduling can expose 27% more usable GPUs in Grace Blackwell systems
item.description: The write-up explains how rack-local NVLink communication in NVL72 systems can avoid slower cross-rack links, and how topology-aware placement can keep jobs local as capacity fragments. These scheduling and resilience trade-offs matter for teams running large training or inference workloads.

item.title: Claude Code review layers checks as daily merges rise above 30,000
item.description: Claude Code's review process uses six layers, from AI and security review through CI and risk-based human approval to staged rollout and rollback; daily merges rose from about 2,500 to over 30,000. The layered controls and reported drop in reverted changes offer a concrete model for keeping review effective as AI-generated code scales.

item.title: Spawn’s agent swarm ships live code hourly at a reported $3 million monthly token cost
item.description: Spawn’s agents modify live code, ship hourly and handle production errors, bug reports, metrics and feature requests; the company reports spending over $3 million in tokens per month. The operating model and cost make this a useful case study in building software with autonomous agents.

item.title: Neki limits write disruption during planned Postgres primary switchovers
item.description: Neki’s switchover process validates a shard, catches a replica up before promotion, and then recovers clients while minimizing the period when writes cannot be routed reliably. These stages offer practical design considerations for planned failovers in distributed databases.

item.title: boAt serves personalized AI coaching to millions of smartwatch users
item.description: boAt’s Bedrock- and Lambda-based AI Coach has been in production for over six months, serving millions of users with plans based on their history and preferences. Its scaling and cost choices offer a production example for teams building personalized AI features.

item.title: Kernel “cells” propose a first-class abstraction for containers
item.description: Linux currently assembles containers from namespaces, cgroups and sandboxing mechanisms rather than recognizing a container object; Josef Bacik’s “cells” proposal revisits that design. The trade-offs matter to engineers working on isolation and container infrastructure.

item.title: System design data movement spans polling, push, queues and change capture
item.description: The guide compares pull, polling, push, long polling, SSE, WebSockets, message queues and change data capture, organized around sources, consumers and triggers. Choosing the right movement pattern matters for correctness and load across distributed systems.

item.title: Meta Andromeda co-designs its retrieval model, system, and GPUs
item.description: Meta says Andromeda scores every eligible ad at retrieval scale with near-ranking-level model performance, using model, system, and GPU co-design. The case offers a useful look at how hardware and model choices interact in a production retrieval system.

item.title: GKE targets high-density networking for concurrent AI sandboxes
item.description: The excerpt describes agent workloads reaching up to one million code-execution sandboxes, with rapid pod churn and a need for sub-second provisioning so accelerators do not wait on sandbox startup. The networking and isolation constraints matter when designing infrastructure for large-scale agent execution.

item.title: Meta PrivacyLib centralizes privacy enforcement at data access boundaries
item.description: PrivacyLib replaces separate implementations of privacy enforcement across data and processing systems with a common library at the data access boundary. Engineers managing cross-system controls can learn from this approach to centralizing policy enforcement.

item.title: Anthropic’s model launches combine product, safety and infrastructure decisions
item.description: Anthropic’s team discusses how growing model capability and API usage affect deployment choices, including the strategic cost of CPU consumed by API requests. The account connects product launches with the infrastructure and access decisions that shape AI services.

item.title: Revinate used API Gateway to expose guest data through APIs
item.description: Revinate used Amazon API Gateway and its Portal to expose guest profiles, reservations, and other CDP data to hotel properties and partners. The case study offers a real example of API infrastructure supporting a growing data platform.

item.title: Anthropic separates agent models, harnesses and sandboxes to scale managed agents
item.description: The discussion covers decoupling the model from its harness and sandbox, with isolation, credentials and network controls for managed agents. Those boundaries are central to scaling agent platforms while limiting what an agent can access.

item.title: Nitro Enclaves provide attested proof of transaction-parser code
item.description: VisualSign runs an open-source transaction parser inside Nitro Enclaves and returns results with attestation-backed evidence of which software produced them. The architecture offers a concrete pattern for verifying code execution in sensitive services.

item.title: Manta trains voyage-optimization models on each vessel’s history
item.description: Manta combines vessel-specific operational histories with forecast weather and ocean conditions to optimize voyages, using AWS data infrastructure. The case illustrates how tailoring models to individual assets can outperform averages in operational ML.

item.title: GLM-5.3 Workers AI responses leaked data across tenants
item.description: Cloudflare says 155 responses to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens contained data from other customers’ requests; it remediated the issue and hardened its SGLang deployments. The incident exposes the isolation risks of shared inference systems.

item.title: NVIDIA Minerva groups 81 alerts into one incident using topology-aware telemetry
item.description: Minerva links GPU, network, storage, and workload telemetry in a live knowledge graph; topology-aware correlation grouped 81 alerts into one incident, saving an estimated 54 hours of cluster uptime. The case shows how infrastructure context and alert correlation can improve GPU fleet operations.

item.title: Entire introduces a Git forge with agent-scored Trails and continuous memory
item.description: Entire combines agent-scored code-review Trails, distributed Git hosting and searchable session and prompt memory; it also claims faster pushes than existing services. The design targets collaboration and infrastructure for agent-driven development.

item.title: Mission Control 2.5 separates Kubernetes job recovery from hardware remediation
item.description: The recovery design restarts or reschedules jobs while hardware recovery quarantines and diagnoses faulty nodes in parallel; transient software errors can be retried without unnecessary hardware action. This separation can limit disruption and avoid misdirected remediation in GPU clusters.

item.title: Salesforce Agentforce has processed 7 billion work units, with instructions once packed into one prompt
item.description: Salesforce reports 7 billion Agentic Work Units across Agentforce and Slack, and says its first Agentforce version put all instructions into one large prompt. The scale and prompt-design challenge make this a useful production agent-platform case.

item.title: Immediate-mode UI can cache unchanged interface work
item.description: The excerpt challenges the assumption that immediate-mode interfaces must repeat expensive work, noting that unchanged UI descriptions may be cached and that sleeping while idle can reduce unnecessary work. These trade-offs matter for responsive, power-conscious desktop and mobile software.

item.title: Shopify revisits React Native as AI coding agents change mobile development economics
item.description: Shopify adopted React Native in 2020 to avoid implementing features separately for Android and iOS, but AI coding agents have since changed the economics of mobile development. The migration is relevant to teams reconsidering platform trade-offs as coding costs shift.

item.title: Matrix’s next-generation timeline uses stitched ordering and state DAGs
item.description: The talk outlines timeline fragments, stitched ordering, and state DAGs as a response to ordering inconsistencies and other Matrix timeline limitations. These design choices matter to engineers building federated chat systems with durable history.

item.title: Block Blast downloads encrypted JavaScript traits after launch
item.description: Reverse engineering found that the app receives a server configuration selecting modular “traits,” then downloads encrypted JavaScript; the examined install selected 254 traits and downloaded 101 after installation. The architecture is a useful look at dynamic code delivery, even though the subject is a game.

item.title: A Flatpak runtime update broke Chromium video playback
item.description: After Chromium’s Flatpak moved to runtime 21.08, users reported broken video playback with audio-renderer errors; the issue escaped the author’s testing because they rarely used desktop YouTube. The case highlights how runtime changes can expose gaps in test coverage.

item.title: Cerebras maps trillion-parameter models across wafer-scale chips
item.description: The deployment write-up describes fitting a roughly 3-trillion-parameter model across multiple 44 GB wafers and claims 1,000–2,000+ tokens per second. The mapping and concurrency approach is directly relevant to engineers weighing large-model serving architectures.

item.title: Animations make metastability and lost writes easier to understand
item.description: The piece uses animations to build intuition about system behavior, including how a Raft cluster can lose writes. Engineers can apply the technique to make distributed-system failure modes easier to reason about.

item.title: Bayer adds a natural-language agent layer to its governed ML workflow platform
item.description: Bayer built an Agentic Decision Engine over its Connected Decision Engine, which deploys, orchestrates, monitors, and reuses ML workflows with execution history and operational controls. The case shows how a multi-agent interface can help users investigate results across a complex workflow platform.

item.title: Google builds Agent Compute Engine as a compute foundation for AI agents
item.description: Google frames agent workloads as a new infrastructure shift, following earlier architecture efforts for web-scale computing, deep learning and cloud security. The piece is relevant to engineers evaluating what compute and storage foundations agent workloads may require.

item.title: Google Cloud targets virtual development from vehicle infotainment to MCUs
item.description: The post describes the gap between cloud-native development for vehicle infotainment and the physical-chip testing still common for smaller control modules. Virtualizing more of the vehicle stack could reduce dependence on benches, samples and hardware rigs.
